title: Extremal subcurve degree for a generically trivial line on a nodal trait
statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $K$ and closed point $s$. Let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a projective flat finitely presented family with nonempty connected reduced one-dimensional geometric fibres, having only ordinary nodes, as in [lem-sfb-nodal-log-canonical-reconstruction] without markings or positivity. Let $T$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] whose restriction to $X_K$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal O_{X_K}$. For any geometric closed fibre $C=X\times_R\Omega$, where $\Omega$ is an algebraic closure of the residue field of $R$, either $T|_C\simeq\mathcal O_C$, or there is a nonempty proper reduced union $Y$ of irreducible components of $C$ such that
$$\deg_Y(T|_C)\geq k_Y>0.$$
The integer $k_Y$ counts the nodes where $Y$ meets the reduced union of the other components; $\deg_Y$ is the sum of degrees on its normalized components [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. This conclusion allows singular total spaces, nodes persisting in the generic fibre, and arbitrary thickness at the nodes which smooth. It does not assume that individual components of the special fibre are Cartier divisors.

proof.text: Write $k=\kappa(s)$ and $L=T|_C$. The projective morphism $f$ is proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. All its residue and geometric fibres are projective by [lem-pc-projective-base-change], hence proper by the same properness lemma. Both $T$ and $\mathcal O_X$ are finitely presented and flat over $R$: locally $T$ is $\mathcal O_X$, and $\mathcal O_X$ is $R$-flat by the given flatness of $f$. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-flat-sheaf-euler-local-constancy] to each of these two modules. A locally constant function on $\operatorname{Spec}R$ has the same value at the generic and closed points, because every open neighbourhood of the closed point contains the generic point. Since $T_K\simeq\mathcal O_{X_K}$, their Euler characteristics agree generically and hence on the closed fibre. The base-change clause of the same lemma carries this equality to $\Omega$. Thus $\chi(C,L)=\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$ and $\deg_C L=0$ by [def-pc-degree-line-bundle].

source.place: Tag 0B9T, lemma-chi-locally-constant-geometric; degree defined in varieties.tex Tag 0AYR.

proof.text: There is a nonzero section $\sigma\in H^0(C,L)$. Indeed $1\in H^0(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})$ is nonzero since the generic fibre is nonempty; the generic trivialization of $T$ therefore gives $\beta^0(\eta)\geq1$. Apply the upper semicontinuity clause of [thm-pc-semicontinuity-base-change], with the properness, finite presentation and relative flatness verified in Step 1. The closed set $\{t:\beta^0(t)\geq1\}$ contains the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, so contains the closed point too. Hence $H^0(X_s,T_s)\ne0$. Apply [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] in degree zero to the flat field extension $k\to\Omega$ and the proper (therefore quasi-compact and quasi-separated) $k$-scheme $X_s$. It identifies $H^0(C,L)$ with $H^0(X_s,T_s)\otimes_k\Omega$, which is nonzero: a nonzero vector extends to a basis and remains nonzero after extension of scalars. Choose $\sigma\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 0BDN, lemma-jump-loci-geometric (upper semicontinuity); coherent.tex Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology.

proof.text:
Let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_v$ be the reduced irreducible components of $C$. By [lem-trf-degree-weighted-irreducible-components] this is a finite list of integral proper curves. Their multiplicities are $1$, since $C$ is reduced and its local ring at each generic point is a field. Let $
u_i:\widetilde Z_i	o Z_i$ be the normalization and put $L_i=
u_i^*(L|_{Z_i})$ and $\sigma_i=
u_i^*(\sigma|_{Z_i})$. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-normalization-adjunction] to the nodal finite-type $\Omega$-curve $C$ and each proper component: $\widetilde Z_i$ is smooth, proper and connected, normalization is an isomorphism over the smooth locus of $Z_i$, and the two branches of each node give two points on the relevant normalizations. In particular a node joining different components has exactly one preimage on each of them. Degree is unchanged by each normalization: $Z_i$ (an integral closed subscheme of the projective $\Omega$-scheme $C$, of dimension one) and $\widetilde Z_i$ (smooth, proper and connected, hence integral) are proper curves over $\Omega$, and $
u_i$ is an isomorphism over the smooth locus of $Z_i$, a dense open since the singular points of $Z_i$ are finitely many self-nodes. So $
u_i$ is dominant with function-field degree $d=1$, and [lem-sfb-proper-curve-bundle-pullback-degree] gives $\deg L_i=\deg(L|_{Z_i})$. Together with the component formula and Step 1 this gives $\sum_i\deg L_i=\deg_C L=0$. Set $I=\{i:\sigma_i
e0\}$. It is nonempty: on an affine trivialization of $L$, a section vanishing at every component's generic point lies in every minimal prime, hence in the nilradical, which is zero because $C$ is reduced.

source.place: Tags 0AYW (lemma-degree-in-terms-of-components) and 0AYZ (lemma-degree-pullback-map-proper-curves, degree one); curves.tex Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), normalization branch description.

proof.text: First suppose $I=\{1,\ldots,v\}$. On each integral proper curve $\widetilde Z_i$, [lem-trf-curve-section-degree-positivity] gives $\deg L_i\geq0$, and gives strict positivity if $\sigma_i$ has any zero. The sum in Step 3 is zero, so every degree is zero and every $\sigma_i$ is nowhere vanishing. Thus $\sigma$ has no zero on $C$: a smooth point of a component has a preimage under its normalization, and at a node its branch preimages exist by Step 3; vanishing of $\sigma$ would force vanishing at any such preimage. These smooth points and nodes cover $C$. Locally in a basis of $L$, the section is consequently a unit in every local ring. Multiplication by $\sigma$ therefore defines an isomorphism $\mathcal O_C\simeq L$. This is the first alternative.

source.place: Tag 0B40, lemma-check-invertible-sheaf-trivial (1), (2), on the normalized components.

proof.text: Otherwise let $Y=\bigcup_{i\in I}Z_i$ and $W=\bigcup_{i\notin I}Z_i$, with reduced structures. Both are nonempty closed unions, and $Y$ is proper as a subcurve of $C$. They can meet only at nodes: a smooth point lies on just one component. If they did not meet, they would be disjoint nonempty open-and-closed subsets covering $C$, contradicting connectedness. At a node there are exactly two branches by the normalization statement in Step 3. Hence each node of $Y\cap W$ has exactly one branch in $Y$. Denote the finite set of these nodes by $B$, so $k_Y=|B|>0$. For $i\in I$ let $B_i\subset\widetilde Z_i$ be its branch preimages over $B$ and set $r_i=|B_i|$. Distinct boundary nodes have distinct preimages, and the branch count gives $\sum_{i\in I}r_i=k_Y$. The section on every component of $W$ is zero, since it is zero at its generic point and the component is integral. Therefore its value in the fibre $L\otimes\kappa(p)$ is zero for every $p\in B$; pulling that value back shows that $\sigma_i$ vanishes at every point of $B_i$.

source.place: Tag 0C4D, lemma-nodal, two-branch description already supplied by Step 3; elementary connectedness and section restriction argument.

proof.text: For each $i\in I$, the smooth connected curve $\widetilde Z_i$ has a DVR at every closed point by [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings]. Thus the finite set $B_i$ defines a reduced effective Cartier divisor $D_i=\sum_{q\in B_i}[q]$: its ideal is generated by a uniformizer at each $q$ and is the unit ideal elsewhere. These branch points are $\Omega$-rational (their branch local model is $\Omega[[u]]$). Because $\sigma_i$ vanishes at them, it is a section $\tau_i$ of $L_i\otimes\mathcal O(-D_i)$: in a local basis its coefficient lies in the point ideal, and off $D_i$ that ideal is the unit ideal, so these local factorizations agree. This section is nonzero since its image is $\sigma_i\ne0$. By [lem-trf-curve-section-degree-positivity], $\deg(L_i\otimes\mathcal O(-D_i))\geq0$. The rational-point and effective-divisor formulas of [lem-pc-degree-base-change], applied with $\mathcal L=L_i\otimes\mathcal O(-D_i)$ and $\mathcal M=\mathcal O(D_i)$, give $\deg L_i=\deg(L_i\otimes\mathcal O(-D_i))+r_i\geq r_i$. This includes $B_i=\varnothing$, when the twist is trivial and $r_i=0$. Summing over $i\in I$ proves $\deg_Y L=\sum_{i\in I}\deg L_i\geq\sum_{i\in I}r_i=k_Y>0$. This is the second alternative and finishes the proof.
